name: scroll-progress
description: A reading-progress bar that grows from the start edge as the page — or the nearest scrolling pane — scrolls. One empty element and a scroll timeline: no script, no scroll listener. Painted in the theme's accent gradient, pinned top or bottom, and absent where scroll timelines are unsupported.

--scroll-progress-color.description: Fill of the bar: a colour token or a gradient (custom property).

a11y.notes: Decorative duplicate of information the scrollbar already exposes, so it is hidden from assistive technology and takes no pointer events. It moves only with the reader's own scrolling, never on a clock, and therefore stays under prefers-reduced-motion.

notes: One page-scoped bar per page, anywhere in <body> — it is position: fixed and pins itself.
data-scope="nearest" makes it sticky inside the nearest scroll container: put it first in that container (or last, with data-variant="bottom").
Under a sticky site header, the header covers a top bar; use data-variant="bottom", or place the bar inside the header.
The fill reads --gradient-accent when the theme defines one, so it matches gradient highlights and glows on the same page.
